blocks.text: Start from the demand, then drill into the cause.

items: On **Demand Summary APS**, find the demand and read **Days Late**, **Due Date**, and **Projected Date**.
Open **Demand Detail** for the demand. The critical path is bold; the cause of the delay shows in red. Expand the job usages to see every contributing supply.
If an item is the holdup, open **Item Bottlenecks APS** — it lists the demands delayed because that item is on their critical path.
If material is missing, open **Component Shortage APS** — anything **APS** could not peg to inventory shows here as short.

blocks.text: Fix the cause, not the date: expedite the bottleneck item, move the purchase order in, or flex capacity — then re-run **APS** and confirm the projected date recovers.

blocks.text: Review exception messages daily on **Planning Detail** (filter the **Exception Message** column) or the **Exceptions** report. Priority 00 is the highest.

head: Message
What it means
What to do
rows: **APS** used the item's expedited lead time to build this receipt, saving N days. A parenthesized Late N means the parent demand is still late by N days.
Confirm the vendor can expedite, or accept and re-promise the late date.
**APS** reallocated this supply from a later demand to an earlier one; the purchase order is needed earlier.
Move the PO in to the suggested date. **APS** will not create another **PLN** if you do.
The demand moved out; this supply arrives earlier than needed.
Move the PO out to the suggested date.
The receipt can be dropped without inventory falling below safety stock.
The receipt will arrive N days after it is needed.
Expedite, find another source, or re-promise.

blocks.text: A message that keeps coming back is a parameter or process problem, not bad luck — fix the root cause.

blocks.text: **APS** plans from the data in the system. Inaccurate data does not just blur the plan — it moves projected dates, creates phantom shortages, and hides real ones.

items: Record labor and material transactions promptly and accurately.
Keep routings and bills of material up to date.
Give purchased items accurate lead times. Inflated lead times push projected dates out and drag every dependent supply with them.
